title: Continuous Product Discovery
content:
Original paraphrased demo notes based on Teresa Torres's Lenny's Podcast episode. These are not verbatim transcript excerpts.

Teresa Torres explains continuous discovery as a sustainable habit of keeping customer learning close to everyday product decisions. The central idea is to build recurring feedback loops instead of treating research as a one-time project phase.

A useful structure is the opportunity solution tree: start from an outcome, map the customer opportunities that could contribute to it, generate multiple solution ideas, and then run small experiments to learn which path is promising. The tree keeps teams from jumping directly from a request to a single feature.

Torres emphasizes that discovery should happen continuously, not only before a roadmap is written. Weekly customer conversations can provide a steady stream of evidence. The goal is not to interview customers for its own sake, but to reduce uncertainty around which problems are worth solving and which solutions are likely to create value.

For feature-factory environments, the practical shift is to frame work around outcomes and opportunities rather than a fixed list of features. A team can still deliver quickly while making customer evidence part of the normal operating rhythm.

Customer interviews should focus on real past behavior and concrete experiences rather than asking people to predict what they might do in the future. Product teams should also separate the opportunity from their preferred solution so that research does not become a search for confirmation.

Key themes: continuous discovery, opportunity solution trees, weekly customer conversations, outcome-oriented product work, evidence-based decisions, and avoiding solution bias.
